name: The Caro-Kann Defense
description: The rock-solid counterpunch for Black against 1. e4. Prepare an unshakeable pawn structure, strike in the center, and easily activate all minor pieces.

steps.title: White Claims Center
steps.explanation: White takes the center with e4, preparing active piece play.

steps.title: The Caro-Kann Setup
steps.explanation: The signature move of the Caro-Kann! We prepare to challenge White's e4 pawn with ...d5 on our next move, supported by the c6 pawn.
steps.warning: Unlike the French Defense (1... e6), the c6 pawn doesn't trap our Light-squared Bishop on c8!

steps.title: White Builds Full Center
steps.explanation: White occupies the center with both pawns (d4 and e4).

steps.title: Strike at e4
steps.explanation: Boom! We strike the center. White must now choose: defend with Nc3, push e5 (Advance), or take on d5.

steps.title: The Classical Setup
steps.explanation: White develops a Knight and guards the e4 pawn.

steps.title: Eliminate the e4 Pawn
steps.explanation: We capture on e4! White is forced to recapture with their Knight, freeing up the c8-h3 diagonal for our Bishop.

steps.title: White Recaptures
steps.explanation: White brings their Knight to a strong central outpost on e4.

steps.title: The Free Bishop!
steps.explanation: We develop our light-squared Bishop with tempo by attacking White's e4 knight. This is the ultimate dream of the Caro-Kann — our bishop is active outside the pawn chain before we play ...e6!
steps.warning: Never play 4... e6 first! That locks the bishop behind the pawn chain forever.
